The bug is fixed: `python3 -c "from shop.cli import main; main(['quote','a:12.5:2'])"` now prints **27.06**, and all 9 tests pass.

**Root cause:** `to_cents` in `shop/money.py:9` padded the cents with zeros on the left (`rjust`) instead of the right (`ljust`). So `"12.5"` was read as `"12.05"`, which is 1205 cents instead of 1250. The last commit (`02a3a46 seed`) introduced this by changing `ljust` to `rjust`.

| | Unit price | × 2 | + 8.25% tax | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 1205 | 2410 | 199 | **26.09** |
| After | 1250 | 2500 | 206 | **27.06** |

Only prices with exactly one decimal place were wrong; `"12.34"` and `"12"` came out right. No test called `to_cents`, so the suite still passed with the bug.

**Changes (not committed):**
- `shop/money.py`: changed `rjust` back to `ljust`. That one line is the fix.
- `tests/test_money.py` (new): three tests for `to_cents`. They cover one decimal, two decimals, none, and the error on three decimals. I also ran them against the old code, and the one-decimal test fails there with `1205 != 1250`.

**Tests:** `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` ran 9 tests (the 6 existing plus the 3 new) and all passed.

`python3 -m shop` doesn't run at all because there is no `shop/__main__.py`, so I used the fallback command you gave. I can add that file if you want the short form to work.

I also found a separate bug in the same function and left it alone. Negative prices with decimals come out wrong: `"-12.5"` would give -1150 instead of -1250, and `"-0.5"` would give +50. That's probably harmless if prices are never negative.
